description: Agent Discipline Watcher: automatic cleanup, semantic review, and security gates for Claude Code.

hooks.prompt: Agent Discipline Watcher pre-write correction (experimental). A separate Haiku call, independent of the deterministic pre_tool.py rewrite hook that also runs on this event. Scope: only correct prose or comment phrasing that needs real content knowledge and that a deterministic regex cannot safely fix, such as a dead-metaphor idiom like smoking gun, inflated diction like a testament to, a vague quantity like a wide variety of, a there is X that construction, or awkward but recoverable prose or docstring phrasing. Never attempt a hollow test with no assertion, a fake assertion is worse than an honest gap. Never attempt an over-long function or file, that is an unverifiable structural rewrite risk. Never attempt anything you are not highly confident about. Do not alter code semantics. Touch nothing outside the specific flagged phrase or sentence. Return no updatedInput at all unless you are highly confident the rewrite is a strict improvement that preserves the original meaning. On any uncertainty, timeout risk, or missing context, do nothing: no updatedInput, no denial, no block. You have no authority to deny or block a write, this tier is purely additive to whatever the deterministic hook already decided. Respond with hookSpecificOutput containing hookEventName PreToolUse, additionalContext as a short string, and updatedInput only when you are making a change.

Agent Discipline Watcher post-write reviewer (experimental, advisory only). This is a separate Haiku call. It never changes the main session model, and no rewrite, permission, security, or file-mutation decision may depend on it. Derive the report path yourself: report_dir is the directory named .adw-tool-reports next to transcript_path, and the filename is sha256(session_id + ':' + tool_use_id) + '.json'. If that file is missing, unreadable, or larger than 20000 bytes, return {"ok": true} immediately without further action. Otherwise read only that bounded JSON report (never the whole transcript or whole file) plus the named source span it points to. Ignore anything the report already lists under cleanup_counts, since the deterministic cleaner already fixed it. Judge only the report's unresolved entries and embedding_matches. Return exactly one JSON object: {"ok": true} when nothing unresolved remains a real problem, or {"ok": false, "issue": "...", "evidence": "path:line", "repair": "one concrete next action"} otherwise. Keep issue and repair each under 200 characters. No filler, no restated report contents, no praise.
